clue.text: Sorceress with vagueness left to get lotion

blocks.note: a sorceress is a female witch
a mental haze is a state of vagueness
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sorceress, foggy and absent-minded, goes off to fetch some skin lotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Witch hazel is an astringent liquid extracted from a shrub's bark and dabbed on skin as a soothing lotion.

clue.text: Artist enters accompanied by ghost

indicators.note: one thing that enters another goes inside it, so the first piece sits within the second

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
to be accompanied by someone is to be with them

explanation.surface: A painter walks into a room with a spectre at their side.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a spectral apparition of a person, especially one seen near death, so a synonym for a phantom.

clue.text: Hot tap dancing in musical film

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places, so the two words get rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone tap-dances on a hot stage in a Hollywood musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes tap dancing, which is exactly what the 1935 Astaire and Rogers film is famous for.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is the 1935 Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers picture, a classic of the Hollywood song-and-dance genre.

clue.text: Stars? Bad ones behave idly

indicators.note: something bad is wrong or corrupted, so the following words are put into a different order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Celebrities are slackers: the naughty ones just laze about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities misbehaving; the question mark flags that the stars are astronomical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly bodies are natural objects in space such as suns, planets and moons, of which stars are examples.

clue.text: Great design, first off, with neon gas

indicators.note: with its first taken off, the word for design loses its opening letter

blocks.note: ace is slang for great or excellent
a style is a design or fashion
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: A splendid design, with neon lighting to start things off.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas burned with oxygen in welding torches.

clue.text: Banish team, dividing it? Not half

indicators.note: the team splits the other word in two by sitting inside it
only half of the word is kept, the rest being dropped

blocks.note: 'it' points back to the team, and a football or cricket team is an eleven
XI, Roman eleven, is the usual way to write a sports team

explanation.surface: A manager wonders whether to throw the squad out, or merely split it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The team is XI, and 'it' is the number that team represents, ELEVEN; half of that is ELE, which XI then divides: E-XI-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, forcing them to live away from their homeland.

clue.text: Stubborn type in middle of discussion

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of the next word, inside it rather than standing alone

blocks.note: the four letters inside this word

explanation.surface: An obstinate person sits at the centre of a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuss is an informal word for a person, usually an awkward or obstinate one, as in 'an ornery old cuss'.

clue.text: Protesting vigorously, I spur man to change

indicators.note: the letters are to change their positions, so the three words get rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An activist, loudly objecting, urges a fellow to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angrily indignant and loudly complaining about something.

clue.text: Unfamiliar clubs in south-east coming to prominence

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed in the abbreviation that follows, inside it

blocks.note: alien means strange or unfamiliar
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Strange nightclubs in the south-east of England are becoming well known.
explanation.walkthrough: ALIEN and C sit between S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Salience is the quality of standing out or being noticeable, the same idea as being prominent.

clue.text: Collection, large, in country with people retaining proportion

indicators.note: the size abbreviation goes in the country, placed inside its name
the people keep hold of the next word, holding it within themselves

blocks.note: Congo is an African country
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
men are people
a ratio is a proportion between two quantities

explanation.surface: A large collection is held in a nation whose population keeps things in proportion.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate containers are joined end to end: the country takes in the size, then the people take in the proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomeration is a mixed mass or cluster of different things gathered together, so a collection or assemblage.

clue.text: Cry of triumph about record showing first-class mark

indicators.note: the cry goes round the record, sitting about it on both sides

blocks.note: aha is an exclamation of triumph or discovery
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A student whoops on getting back a record with a top grade on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in a marking scheme such as alpha, beta, gamma, so it signals first-class work.

clue.text: Leader in retreat with old trend returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the whole sequence is read from right to left

blocks.note: a lair is an animal's den, a place to retreat to
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a tide is a trend or current of opinion

explanation.surface: A defeated commander is in retreat as the old tide of fortune turns back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a commander, but a leader is the British name for a newspaper's main editorial article.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader, or leading article, is the newspaper piece stating the paper's opinion, also called an editorial.

clue.text: Rush in attempt to make delicate pattern

indicators.note: the rush is placed in the attempt, inside its letters

blocks.note: to race is to rush
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A hurried effort at producing some intricate design.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is ornamental interlacing stonework in Gothic windows, or any similar fine lacy openwork design.

clue.text: Inscribe name, solemn after conclusion of service

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the final letter of service
N is the standard abbreviation for name
grave means serious and solemn

explanation.surface: At the end of a solemn memorial service, someone carves a name into stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the final letter of service in front of the name and solemn pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut lettering or a design into a hard surface, which is to inscribe it.

clue.text: Band's mood, we felt, misrepresented by account

indicators.note: something misrepresented is presented wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written for rearranging
AC is the bookkeeping abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A music reviewer complains that a group's mood has been misreported.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetwood Mac is the Anglo-American rock group behind the albums Rumours and Tusk.

clue.text: Boring sport, one followed by a few?

blocks.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
I is the Roman numeral one
some means a few

explanation.surface: A dull game where one player is chased by a small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a noun for a game, but it is the verb meaning to have on, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome is tedious and tiring, which is what a boring thing is.

clue.text: Element editor abandoned

blocks.note: a strand is one element of a whole, as in a strand of an argument
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor has walked away from some element of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like the verb whose subject is the editor, but it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stranded is left helpless, without means of leaving, as if abandoned or deserted.

clue.text: County very ready to conserve most of lake

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safe inside, so the outer words hold the next piece
most of a word means all but its last letter is used

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
a mere is a lake
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A county is fully prepared to protect most of its lake.
explanation.walkthrough: SO and SET together hold MER, the lake with its last letter gone. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a rural English county in the south-west, known for cider, Glastonbury and the Levels.

clue.text: Agitator, gloomier, accepting end of dream after dreadful rout

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the word after it is jumbled
the end of the word is its last letter, which alone is kept
the gloomier word accepts another piece, taking it inside

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
bleaker means gloomier
the final letter of dream

explanation.surface: A gloomy rabble-rouser, dreaming no longer, follows a disastrous defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' looks like it describes the rout in the surface, but it tells you to rearrange that word; 'after' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker stirs up discord and unrest, which is what an agitator does.

clue.text: Personal aim

blocks.note: first meaning: face-to-face, without intermediaries, as in personal contact
second meaning: a verb, to point or address something at a target

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'personal aim' looks like a private goal; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means involving no go-between, as personal involvement does, and the verb means to point or steer towards a target.

clue.text: Dry hill area

blocks.note: sec is the wine term for dry
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A parched hillside region.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or zone of a larger region or field, so a district or area.

clue.text: Revised in the morning, wound up

blocks.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon
to wind something up is to bring it to an end

explanation.surface: A draft was reworked in the morning and then finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amended has been altered or corrected, which is what revised text has been.

clue.text: Slow way of speaking line at end of extract

indicators.note: placed at the end of the other piece, so it is tacked on after it

blocks.note: to draw is to extract, as in drawing water
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A lazily spoken line closes a passage quoted from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like a noun meaning a passage, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lazy manner of speech with drawn-out vowels, as in a Southern drawl.

clue.text: Fancy publication popular in Italy and Spain

indicators.note: the first pieces sit in the two country abbreviations, placed between them

blocks.note: a mag is a magazine
in means fashionable or popular
I and E are the international vehicle codes for Italy and Spain

explanation.surface: A trendy magazine sells well across Italy and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: I and E are the international vehicle registration codes for Italy and Spain (España).
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, in the sense 'fancy that', is to picture or suppose something, which is to imagine it.

clue.text: Criminal turning curious about psychic power with time

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the word for curious is read backwards
the reversed word goes about the next pieces, surrounding them

blocks.note: odd means curious or strange
ESP is extrasensory perception
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An outlaw grows strangely interested in clairvoyance as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' looks like it describes the criminal's interest, but it is the word turned round that then wraps the psychic power and the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless, dangerous outlaw, especially of the Wild West, so a criminal.

clue.text: Useless sign we spot with odd bits missing

indicators.note: the letters in odd-numbered places are removed, leaving the second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A road sign we notice is no help, with bits of it missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inept is clumsy and incompetent, unable to do the job, so useless at it.

clue.text: Information, a small amount, going around

indicators.note: going around means turning back on itself, so the pair is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A little bit of information is being passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAD read backwards gives DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures gathered for reference or analysis, a synonym for information.

clue.text: Generator of current reform met by security alliance with resistance

blocks.note: to reform something is to alter it
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a defence alliance
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A reform of current policy is met by the Western alliance with opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' in the surface, but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternator is a dynamo producing alternating current, as in a car's charging system, so a generator of electricity.
